perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals
observations: Lockheed Martin reported second-quarter 2026 sales of $20.1B, up 11% year over year, $65B of new orders and record backlog of $230B; management raised 2026 sales and free-cash-flow guidance.

A September 17, 2026 framework agreement with the U.S. Department of War targets accelerated AIM-260/JATM production, adding a fresh production-scale signal beyond the earlier PAC-3/THAAD/PrSM expansion frameworks.
September 10 Space Force task orders add $114M of GPS ground-segment modernization work, reinforcing continuing demand across missile and space infrastructure rather than a single-program signal.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution
observations: Execution evidence improved materially from Q1: Q2 free cash flow was $2.9B and management projected 2026 free cash flow of roughly $7.0-$7.2B and sales of roughly $79.75-$81.75B.
The production thesis depends on converting framework agreements and backlog into funded awards, capacity, deliveries and margins; announced demand is not equivalent to realized production economics.

The strongest near-term falsifier is failure to translate record backlog and multi-year production frameworks into sustained delivery growth/cash conversion without renewed program charges or material schedule/cost deterioration.

contradictions: Q1 2026 free cash flow was negative $291M while Q2 rebounded to $2.9B; timing of customer receipts materially affects quarter-to-quarter cash conversion, so one strong quarter should not be extrapolated mechanically.
unknowns: economic terms and funded quantities under the September 17 JATM framework
incremental capital required and margin profile for the accelerated missile ramps
portion and timing of the $230B backlog converting to revenue beyond disclosed guidance
whether future program charges emerge as production rates scale

sources.use: current operating performance, backlog, orders and guidance
